topics.topic_name: Python programming fundamentals (syntax, data types, control flow, functions, I/O, string/list/dict/tuple/set operations, mutability, scope)

resources.title: Learn Python - Full Course for Beginners
resources.why_recommended: A complete 4.5-hour beginner course covering syntax, data types, control flow, functions, I/O and the core list/dict/tuple/set operations - exactly the Python foundation GATE DA assumes.

resources.title: The Python Tutorial - Data Structures (lists, tuples, dicts, sets)
resources.why_recommended: The authoritative reference for list/dict/tuple/set operations, comprehensions and using lists as stacks/queues, with precise semantics no third party matches.

resources.title: The Python Tutorial - More Control Flow Tools (functions, scope)
resources.why_recommended: Official coverage of control flow, defining functions, default/keyword arguments and variable scope - the exact behaviours (mutability, LEGB scope) GATE tests conceptually.

topics.topic_name: Recursion (structure, base cases, recursion trees, recursive vs iterative equivalence)

resources.title: Algorithms (full playlist)
resources.why_recommended: Abdul Bari's early lectures develop recursion, base cases and recurrence relations (T(n)=T(n-1)+1 etc.) with the clearest step-by-step tracing available for GATE.

resources.title: 1.8.1 Asymptotic Notations Big Oh - Omega - Theta #1
resources.why_recommended: Sets up the growth-rate reasoning needed to analyse recursion trees and prove recursive vs iterative equivalence via recurrences.

resources.title: Recursion - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: A written walkthrough of recursion structure, base/recursive cases and the recursion tree/stack with runnable code and practice problems.

resources.title: 1.8.1 Asymptotic Notations Big Oh - Omega - Theta #1
resources.why_recommended: The definitive clear derivation of Big-O, Big-Omega and Theta with formal definitions and examples - precisely the asymptotic reasoning GATE demands.

resources.title: MIT 6.006 Introduction to Algorithms (Fall 2011)
resources.why_recommended: MIT's canonical algorithms course opens with asymptotic analysis and models of computation, giving rigorous time/space complexity foundations with lecture notes and problem sets.

resources.title: Analysis of Algorithms (Big-O analysis) - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: A written reference on best/average/worst-case and asymptotic notations with worked examples, good for quick revision before the exam.

topics.topic_name: Stacks and Queues (operations, applications, array/linked-list implementation)

resources.title: Data structures: Introduction to stack
resources.why_recommended: mycodeschool's stack introduction cleanly explains LIFO operations, applications and both array and linked-list implementations - a classic beginner reference.

resources.title: CS50x 2023 - Lecture 5 - Data Structures
resources.why_recommended: Harvard CS50's data-structures lecture builds stacks and queues alongside linked lists with vivid explanations of push/pop and enqueue/dequeue.

resources.title: Stack Data Structure - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: A written reference covering stack/queue operations, applications and implementations with code and practice problems.

resources.title: Introduction to linked list
resources.why_recommended: mycodeschool's linked-list introduction is the gold standard for understanding nodes, pointers and arrays-vs-linked-lists trade-offs before pointer manipulation.

resources.title: Data structures (mycodeschool full playlist)
resources.why_recommended: The full playlist works through singly and doubly linked lists - insertion, deletion, reversal and C/C++ pointer implementation - step by step.

resources.title: Linked List Data Structure - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: A comprehensive written hub for singly/doubly linked list operations and pointer manipulation with runnable code and practice sets.

topics.topic_name: Trees (binary trees, BST properties, traversals - inorder/preorder/postorder/level-order, height/depth)

resources.title: Tree (mycodeschool playlist)
resources.why_recommended: mycodeschool's tree playlist covers binary trees, BST properties, all four traversals and height/depth with the clearest intuition and code for beginners.

resources.title: Tree Traversal Techniques (inorder, preorder, postorder) - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: The canonical written reference for the three depth-first traversals plus level-order, with recursion/stack code - directly matching GATE traversal questions.

resources.title: CS50x 2023 - Lecture 5 - Data Structures (Binary Search Trees)
resources.why_recommended: Harvard CS50 motivates binary search trees from arrays and linked lists, making the BST ordering property and its search benefit intuitive.

topics.topic_name: Hash Tables (hashing functions, collision resolution, load factor)

resources.title: CS50x 2023 - Lecture 5 - Data Structures (Hash Tables)
resources.why_recommended: Harvard CS50 introduces hashing, hash functions and collision handling with chaining in an unusually intuitive way for first-time learners.

resources.title: Collision Resolution Techniques - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: Explains separate chaining vs open addressing (linear/quadratic probing, double hashing) and the role of load factor - the exact GATE hashing distinctions.

resources.title: Open Addressing Collision Handling technique in Hashing - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: A focused write-up on open addressing with linear/quadratic probing and double hashing plus load-factor effects, useful for numerical probing problems.

resources.title: Algorithms (full playlist - Searching section)
resources.why_recommended: Abdul Bari explains linear and binary search with clear complexity analysis (O(n) vs O(log n)) and dry runs, ideal for GATE-style reasoning.

resources.title: Binary Search - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: The canonical binary search reference with iterative/recursive code, O(log n) analysis and abundant practice problems.

resources.title: Searching Algorithms - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: A hub page comparing linear and binary search with complexity tables, good for consolidated revision.

topics.topic_name: Elementary sorting (selection sort, bubble sort, insertion sort)

resources.title: Algorithms (full playlist - Sorting section)
resources.why_recommended: Abdul Bari's sorting lectures dry-run bubble, selection and insertion sort with best/worst-case and stability analysis - exactly the depth GATE expects.

resources.title: Comparison among Bubble, Selection and Insertion Sort - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: Directly compares the three elementary sorts on time/space, swaps, comparisons and stability - the property table GATE frequently probes.

resources.title: Bubble Sort Algorithm - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: A worked reference for bubble sort with the optimized early-exit variant and its O(n) best case, useful for pass-count questions.

topics.topic_name: Divide-and-conquer sorting (merge sort, quick sort - including stability and worst/average case)

resources.title: Recursive Merge Sort By Abdul Bari
resources.why_recommended: Abdul Bari derives merge sort with its recursion tree and the T(n)=2T(n/2)+n recurrence giving O(n log n) - the precise divide-and-conquer analysis GATE tests.

resources.title: Algorithms (full playlist - Quick Sort & Merge Sort)
resources.why_recommended: The playlist covers quick sort's partitioning, worst case O(n^2) vs average O(n log n) and merge sort stability - the full comparison GATE asks about.

resources.title: Merge Sort - Data Structure and Algorithms - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: A written reference for merge sort with code, recurrence, stability discussion and practice problems to complement the video derivation.

topics.topic_name: Graph representation and traversal (adjacency list/matrix, BFS, DFS)

resources.title: Graph Theory Algorithms (playlist)
resources.why_recommended: William Fiset (Google engineer) explains adjacency list/matrix representations and animates BFS and DFS with source code - the best free graph-algorithms series.

resources.title: Graph Algorithms for Technical Interviews - Full Course (freeCodeCamp)
resources.why_recommended: A hands-on Python graph course building adjacency-list representations and implementing BFS/DFS from scratch, ideal for the GATE DA Python context.

resources.title: Breadth First Search or BFS for a Graph - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: The canonical BFS reference with queue-based code, O(V+E) analysis and practice problems; pairs with the companion DFS article.

resources.title: Depth First Search or DFS for a Graph - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: The canonical DFS reference with recursion/stack code and O(V+E) analysis, covering the visited-array handling of cycles.

topics.topic_name: Graph shortest-path algorithms (Dijkstra's algorithm; conceptually Bellman-Ford/Floyd-Warshall as extensions)

resources.title: Graph Theory Algorithms (playlist - Dijkstra's shortest path)
resources.why_recommended: William Fiset animates Dijkstra's algorithm (lazy and eager) and covers Bellman-Ford and Floyd-Warshall in the same series - the ideal shortest-path grounding.

resources.title: Algorithms (full playlist - Dijkstra & Greedy shortest paths)
resources.why_recommended: Abdul Bari's greedy-methods lectures dry-run Dijkstra's relaxation step by step and contrast it with Bellman-Ford and Floyd-Warshall.

resources.title: Dijkstra's Shortest Path Algorithm - GeeksforGeeks
resources.why_recommended: The canonical written reference for Dijkstra with priority-queue implementation, complexity analysis and practice problems.
